1.point: The dead have not gone away, and because the way to God runs through the soul, this chapter will show which worlds the soul lives in, how it crosses them, and how deeds give it a form there, so that what it becomes is in our hands.
steps: Explain the opening prayer: sleep stands for neglect, set beside meeting God
Move from sleep to death and the common picture of barzakh as a far-off waiting room
Counter it: the dead do not go anywhere, because of what the soul is; announce the chapter's three steps

2.point: Reality has three depths, matter, images and intellect, and barzakh is the middle one, so the dead have gone deeper, not away.
steps: The soul is a copy of creation, so our three ways of knowing each sample a world
Senses meet the material world; the other two are unseen, not distant
Imagination samples a world of images: shape and colour without matter, existing outside any mind
Intellect samples a world of pure meaning, the world of intellects
The world of images stands between the other two, hence it is barzakh
These worlds are dimensions of one reality, differing in depth not distance
Therefore the dead in barzakh are deeper in this world, not elsewhere

3.point: The soul is made to stand between the worlds and moves among them, and its reach is unfixed, depending on the life it lives.
steps: The soul has a share in each world because it links spirit and body
The body holds the soul's attention; that hold loosens in sleep, death and contemplation
Sleep: the soul touches the world of images (dreams of the future)
Death: the same loosening to a greater degree; the soul goes on in the image body
Contemplation: muraqaba turns attention and lets a person see into the middle world
Angels have fixed stations; the human soul does not
So how far a soul goes depends on the life it lives

4.point: Deeds done now shape the soul and so shape the image body we meet after death.
steps: Objection: if all pass into the middle world, deeds seem to change little
Repeated acts shape the self (habit, lying)
That shaping marks the image body far more than the visible body
Authority: the next-world form is fixed by the soul's state at death
Rewards and punishments can be the deeds themselves made manifest
Therefore the image body is being shaped now

5.point: There is one self with three states, it can be moved from commanding evil to peace by familiar acts, so what the soul becomes is, with God's grace, in our hands.
steps: If deeds give the soul its form, the self is not fixed
The Qur'an names three states: commanding, blaming, at peace
These are one self under different names, so changing attitude changes state
Familiar acts (dhikr, fasting, night prayer) move the self between states
They work because the soul takes on habits, and it is entrusted to us
The drive to begin is God's grace; the rest is our work

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: Explains the opening quotation and sets sleep as a picture of neglect beside the meeting with God; the hook.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Moves from sleep to death and states the common picture (barzakh as a far-off waiting room) the chapter will overturn.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: States the counter-claim ('we don't go anywhere'), gives the reason (the soul), and announces the chapter's three steps.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Supplies the method: soul as a copy of creation, so three ways of knowing sample three worlds.

¶5.label: advance
¶5.why: First world via the senses; also plants 'unseen, not far away', which ¶10 and ¶12 depend on.

¶6.label: support
¶6.why: Example of imagination (friend's face, dream) that ¶7 uses to introduce the world of images.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: Second world: the world of images, existing outside any mind.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: Third world: the world of intellects.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: World of images stands between the other two, hence barzakh; ¶12 needs this to equate the dead's barzakh with the world of images.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: Supplies the decisive step: the worlds differ in depth, not distance.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: Applies depth-not-distance to the graveside: the section's conclusion, first stated here. Resurrection sentence is a small extension.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Soul has a share in each world because it links spirit and body. The excursus on 'His spirit' and the Kaʿba is a side remark inside an otherwise needed paragraph.

¶14.label: advance
¶14.why: Sets the frame: body holds the soul's attention; the hold loosens at three times.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: First loosening, sleep, with the future-dream as evidence that the soul touches the middle world.

¶16.label: support
¶16.why: Lead-in to the Zumar verse that ¶17 reads; one claim (Qur'an pairs sleep and death) which ¶17 uses.

¶17.label: advance
¶17.why: Second loosening, death: difference of degree from sleep, and the image body introduced.

¶18.label: support
¶18.why: Bahmanpour's 'soul carries the body' and 'a soul cannot be without a body' back the death step and are drawn on later (¶24, ¶37). Borderline: the last sentence repeats ¶17.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: Third loosening, contemplation/muraqaba; the Imams remark at the end is a side note.

¶20.label: restate
¶20.why: Summarises the three loosenings already given in ¶15, ¶17, ¶19.

¶21.label: advance
¶21.why: Angels' fixed station is the contrast the point needs for 'the soul's reach is not fixed'.

¶22.label: advance
¶22.why: Section conclusion: human soul has no fixed place; reach depends on the life lived.

¶23.label: advance
¶23.why: Raises the objection and answers the first step: habit shapes the self (lying).

¶24.label: advance
¶24.why: Supplies the key step and in effect states the point: the image body takes the shape of what habits have made of the soul.

¶25.label: support
¶25.why: Khomeini's authority for ¶24's claim, adding that the state at death fixes the form; ¶28 relies on this.

¶26.label: aside
¶26.why: A hadith and a verse about the Last Day groups and their light; ¶27 concedes the Last Day body is not the image body, so this is a second witness saying the same, about a different body. Cutting it leaves ¶28 intact.

¶27.label: support
¶27.why: First half continues the Last Day detour; second half supplies Shomali's 'rewards are the actions themselves', which ¶28 uses. Kept for that principle.

¶28.label: restate
¶28.why: Restates ¶24's conclusion ('the image body is being shaped now') by a second route, with a further Shomali quotation. The conclusion is stated twice in the section.

¶29.label: restate
¶29.why: Summary of sections 2-4 before the section begins.

¶30.label: advance
¶30.why: Self is not fixed; three Qur'anic names read as states; the first state introduced.

¶31.label: support
¶31.why: Reads the Yusuf verse (mercy overcomes this self, used by ¶39's grace sentence) and adds worry as a bodily pull, which ¶38 uses ('trained to worry about the body').

¶32.label: advance
¶32.why: Second state, the blaming self, and why it is hopeful.

¶33.label: advance
¶33.why: Third state, the self at peace.

¶34.label: advance
¶34.why: Core step: these are one self, so changing attitude changes state.

¶35.label: advance
¶35.why: Supplies the step 'familiar acts move the self': dhikr.

¶36.label: support
¶36.why: Root link between the Raʿd verse and mutmaʾinna ties dhikr to the third state; ¶35 needs it to land.

¶37.label: support
¶37.why: Further examples of the same step (fasting, night prayer), linked to the loosening of section 3; ¶38 refers back to 'these acts'.

¶38.label: advance
¶38.why: Why the acts work (habit) and the elastic image; the soul is entrusted to us, which the point needs.

¶39.label: restate
¶39.why: Chapter summary. The one new link, that the drive to begin is God's grace, is buried in it; the rest repeats ¶12, ¶20, ¶28, ¶34.

¶40.label: aside
¶40.why: A question raised and not answered; the argument does not use it.
